subject: Insurance
title: San Francisco 1906
description: A quick, practical guide to San Francisco 1906.

hook.text: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake killed 3,000 people.

buildup.text: Broken gas mains ignited fires across the city.

discovery.text: Most policies covered fire but not earthquakes. Homeowners set their own homes on fire to trigger insurance payouts.

twist.text: Insurers fought millions in claims. Some refused to pay, arguing the earthquake—not fire—caused the true damage.

climax.text: San Francisco forced the creation of earthquake-specific insurance.

quiz.question: Why did San Francisco homeowners set their own houses on fire in 1906?
options: Policies covered fire but not earthquakes
